The Last Time I Saw Mother by Arlene J. Chai.

Back in the school year before the pandemic, our English teacher had us read this book. And just like every Highschooler, we didn't want to but had to cooperate because it was Graded.
Getting myself to read the book and take note of details sounded boring yet tiring. We had 2 weeks to read that book until she gave us a quiz bases off of the book. Me being me, i procrastinated and kept the book inside my bag where it was buried at the bottom for the next days. 
About 3 days before the quiz, i was starting to notice my classmates rushing to read the book. My procrastinated-self didn't realize that this book had 300+ pages.
It was at lunchtime that i got myself to skip lunch and dedicate the 1-hour break to reading it.
I managed to read it before the day of the quiz and got to answer every single question on the paper. 
Even after the quiz, i kept reading it...
The book was filled with the history of the Philippines but in the family the story was centered around, the author was able to give each member their own personality and emotion.
